# Skelpr

> Repository evidence with file:line citations, within a context budget.
> Connect a coding agent over MCP or use the standalone CLI with a configured
> generation provider. In MCP mode, the agent decides when to call Skelpr.

## Setup and data handling

- Python 3.10+. Standard setup uses Docker for PostgreSQL, Qdrant and isolated
  validation. External database services are supported.
- Configure an embedding endpoint for semantic search. Standalone generation
  needs a separate model provider. From 0.3.6, plain pip install skelpr includes
  CLI and MCP support.
- Running requires activation. Each activated machine uses one license seat;
  managed leases check in during use.
- Hosted embeddings receive indexed text and queries. Standalone generation
  receives prompts and selected source context. Optional Langfuse tracing can
  include source and outputs. The coding agent has its own data policy.
- Context limits can exclude relevant evidence. Check reported gaps and request
  more context when needed. Empty search results do not prove absence.

## Case studies

- Sock Shop: the historical report claimed 59% fewer tokens and 76% fewer file
  reads. Retained artifacts do not fully reconcile with the published aggregate.
- Django, ten Codex tasks: total tokens 437,997 to 274,749 (37.27% fewer), native
  search/read calls 28 to 9, combined rubric score 89/96 to 91/96. Total wall time
  was 534.40 to 521.25 seconds; four tasks were slower with Skelpr.
- Django totals include cached input and output tokens. These are retained
  matched comparisons across successive builds; the questions informed tuning.
  Q8 and Q10 used seeded defects. Neither study establishes general performance
  or results for one frozen release.
